I am 48 years old. I started helping my father in the fields when I was 8, so I have been farming for 40 years now. I only finished primary school, but I know my land well. I have 60 mu in Quzhou County. My household has 4 people — me, my wife, and two kids. My wife and I do most of the farm work, but one of my sons works in the county town and sends money back when he can.

Last year I planted 25 mu of wheat in the winter, then summer maize on the same land after the wheat harvest. I also had 30 mu of cotton and 5 mu of spring peanut. It worked out fine, so I will do the same this year. Why change what is working? A bad year would hurt me badly. I have a well, so I can irrigate when I need to, but diesel for the pump costs money, so I count every time I water.

For my **winter wheat** on 25 mu: I use the rotary tiller before sowing. I plant about 26 jin of seed per mu — I buy good improved seed, not the old traditional kind, because the yield is better. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu, and I expect the same this year if the weather holds. I put down 100 kg of compound fertilizer as base — the bag says it has some nitrogen, phosphorus, and a little potassium. Then I topdress with 80 kg of urea per mu because wheat needs nitrogen to fill the grain. I irrigate 3 times: once at sowing to help germination, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. For spraying, I do herbicide once to kill weeds, insecticide once for aphids, and fungicide once to prevent disease. That is 3 sprayings total.

For **summer maize** on the same 25 mu: After the wheat harvest, I do no-tillage planting — I just drill the maize seed straight into the stubble. I use Denghai 605 hybrid seed, about 1.2 bags per mu. This variety is good, my neighbor planted it and got over 1700 jin per mu, so I copied him. I expect about 1720 jin per mu. I put 80 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — this one has more nitrogen and some phosphorus, no potassium. Maize does not need as much water as wheat, so I irrigate twice: once right after sowing, and once at the big喇叭口 stage. I spray herbicide once, insecticide once, and fungicide once — 3 times total.

For **spring peanut** on 5 mu: This is my small plot. I use the rotary tiller and plant Haihua variety, about 40 jin of seed per mu. I expect around 550 jin per mu. Peanut needs more care. I put 80 kg of compound fertilizer at sowing — 15-15-15, balanced. Then when the flowers start, I topdress with another 80 kg of compound fertilizer. I irrigate 5 times because peanut likes moist soil, especially when the pods are forming. I spray insecticide 3 times, herbicide once, and fungicide 3 times for leaf spot — that is 7 sprayings.

For **cotton** on 30 mu: This is my biggest crop. I rotary till and plant Minfeng 12 improved seed, about 2.5 jin per mu. Last year I got 600 jin per mu of seed cotton, and I hope for the same. Cotton is expensive to manage. I put 100 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then another 80 kg when it starts flowering. I irrigate 4 times — at planting, at flowering, at boll setting, and once more before the bolls open. Cotton pests are terrible. I spray insecticide 9 times, herbicide twice, and fungicide 9 times. That is 20 sprayings total. I know it costs a lot, but if I skip even one spraying, the bollworms will destroy everything.

Some people say I use too much fertilizer, but I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing half my yield. A bad harvest means I cannot pay for my son's wedding or my daughter's school fees. I watch what my neighbors do, and most people around here use similar amounts. My wife says we should be careful with money, and she is right, but on a 60 mu farm, I cannot afford to be cheap on inputs.
